To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MID1-PP2A-α4 complex is a regulator of the transcription factor GL3 and that point mutations in GLI3, that are associated with GCPS, lead to mislocalization and altered transcriptional activity of the protein.
mutations in GLI3 lead either to a gain or to loss of function by misregulation of GLI3 localization and transcriptional activation.
mutations in the C-terminus of GLI3, that are associated with Greig-cephalo-poly-syndactyli-syndrome, result in misregulation of GLI3-subcellular localization and transcriptional activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the molecular pathomechanisms of malformation syndomes caused by mutations in GLI3, which will provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, and may lead to novel therapeutic approaches.
the molecular basis of human malformation syndrom.
understanding how GLI3-misregulation causes human diseases, and how PP2A and the MID1-ubiquitin ligase complex regulate GLI3 activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PP2A-MID1 complex is a central hub for the regulation of GLI3-subcellular localization and thus transcriptional activity.
the PP2A-MID1 complex is a central player in the regulation of GLI3 activity, which in turn is a key player in the regulation and control of embryogenesis.
the PP2A-MID1-α4 complex regulates the nuclear localization of GLI3, and that GCPS-associated mutations lead to misregulated GLI3 localization, which is the molecular basis for the GCPS-phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PP2A-MID1-complex regulates the subcellular localization of GLI3, and that mutations in the MID1- or GLI3-gene that affect this regulation lead to the development of syndromes with overlapping phenotypes.

PP2A is a key player in the regulation of GLI3-subcellular localization and function and thus in the control of normal embryonic patterning and organogenesis, as well as in the pathogenesis of several human syndromes.
GLI3-mutation and dysregulated PP2-activity lead to the same phenotype by affecting GLI3 localization and transcriptional output in a similar way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

GLI3-mutants that are not linked to loss-of-function, but to misregulation in its subcellular localization may be a more common cause of GCPS and PHS, and that the PP2A-MID1-GLI3 interaction is a key player in that process.

the PP2A-MID1 complex regulates GLI3 localization and transcriptional activation in a region between amino acids 568-1101 of GLI3, and that point mutations that are located in the region between amino acids (a.a.) 569 and 1101 of GLi3 lead to misregualtion of the GLI3 subnuclear localization and transcriptional function.

PP2A- activity is involved in the control of the nuclear localization and the transcriptional activity of the GLI3 protein, and that this is a key event in the pathogenesis of the Greig-cepholopolysyndactly-syndrome.
